title: Employees Sharing the Same Salary
description:
Find all pairs of employees who earn **exactly the same salary** (each distinct pair listed once, with the lower id first).

**Table: employees**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| salary | INT |

Output columns: `employee_1`, `employee_2`, `salary`. Order by `salary`, `employee_1`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, salary INT); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Alice',120000),(2,'Bob',80000),(3,'Carol',120000),(4,'Dan',80000),(5,'Eve',90000),(6,'Fay',120000);
solution_sql: SELECT a.name AS employee_1, b.name AS employee_2, a.salary FROM employees a JOIN employees b ON a.salary = b.salary AND a.id < b.id ORDER BY a.salary, a.name

test_cases.description: Alice-Carol, Alice-Fay, Carol-Fay at 120k; Bob-Dan at 80k

hints: Self join with a.salary = b.salary and a.id < b.id avoids duplicates and self-pairing.
a.id < b.id ensures each pair appears only once.
explanation: Joining employees to themselves on equal salary produces all combinations. The condition `a.id < b.id` prevents (Alice, Alice) and duplicate pairs like (Carol, Alice) and (Alice, Carol). At 120k: (Alice, Carol), (Alice, Fay), (Carol, Fay). At 80k: (Bob, Dan).
